sections.title: Strategy for Spell Check Level 2
sections.content: In Level 2, spelling errors are more subtle and are often related to suffix rules, silent letters, or sentence context. To solve them, follow 3–4 steps: Step 1: Identify the root word. Step 2: Apply the correct suffix or spelling rule. Step 3: Check for silent letters or unusual spelling patterns. Step 4: If a sentence is given, verify the spelling according to the context.

sections.title: Confusing Suffixes: -able vs -ible
sections.content: Step 1: Identify the root word. Step 2: If the root exists as a complete word, the suffix -able is usually used. Step 3: If the root is not clearly identifiable, -ible is often used. Step 4: Compare with correct spelling patterns. Example: indispensable is correct, while permissable is incorrect; the correct spelling is permissible.

sections.title: -ance vs -ence
sections.content: Step 1: Identify the base adjective or verb. Step 2: Check whether the base word ends with 'ant' or 'ent'. Step 3: Accordingly, the noun will use 'ance' or 'ence'. Step 4: Remember common patterns. Example: important → importance, different → difference.

sections.title: -cede vs -ceed
sections.content: Step 1: Check whether the word follows the 'ceed' pattern. Step 2: Generally, 'ceed' appears in only a few words. Step 3: Most other words use 'cede'. Step 4: Identify the correct spelling pattern. Example: proceed, succeed, and exceed use 'ceed', while precede and supersede use 'cede'.

sections.title: Silent Letters and Unusual Clusters
sections.content: Step 1: Identify the pronunciation of the word. Step 2: Check for silent letters such as p, b, t, or k. Step 3: Recognize unusual consonant clusters. Step 4: Compare with the standard spelling. Example: In pneumonia the 'p' is silent, in subtle the 'b' is silent, and in pseudonym the 'p' is silent.

sections.title: Contextual Spelling (Sentence Based)
sections.content: Step 1: Read the entire sentence carefully. Step 2: Check the spelling of the highlighted words. Step 3: Use grammar and context to determine which word is misspelled. Step 4: Identify the correct spelling. Example: He gave a very persistant effort to complete the task. Here 'persistant' is incorrect; the correct spelling is 'persistent'.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content: 1. Choosing the wrong suffix between -able and -ible. 2. Confusion between -ance and -ence. 3. Removing or incorrectly adding silent letters. 4. Selecting spelling without reading the sentence context.

sections.title: Quick Summary
sections.content: In Level 2 spell check questions, suffix rules, silent letters, and contextual understanding are important. To identify the correct spelling, analyze the root word, pronunciation, and sentence context.

tricks.title: ABLE Root Trick
tricks.explanation: If the root word is clearly recognizable, the suffix -able is usually used.

tricks.title: IBLE Memory Trick
tricks.explanation: Some common words use -ible and need to be memorized.

tricks.title: ANT/ENT Rule
tricks.explanation: If the adjective has 'ant', the noun usually takes 'ance', and if it has 'ent', the noun usually takes 'ence'.

tricks.title: Silent Letter Check
tricks.explanation: If a letter is not heard in pronunciation, it may still appear in spelling.

tricks.title: Pseudo Trick
tricks.explanation: Words beginning with 'pseudo' have a silent 'p'.

tricks.title: Cluster Memory
tricks.explanation: Remember difficult consonant clusters using visual memory.

tricks.title: Sentence Check Trick
tricks.explanation: If a sentence is given, check the spelling of each highlighted word one by one.
tricks.example: He made a persistant attempt → 'persistent' is correct.
